title: How Oliver Brocato went from Tabs to Bustm: B2B pricing, personal brand growth and zero churn
summary: Oliver Brocato explains moving from a viral consumer brand (Tabs) to B2B software (Bustm), including how he fixed pricing by switching to a performance model with a monitoring fee. He covers founder-led growth through his Twitter, word of mouth, and why a good product beats marketing machines in B2B.

principles.text: In B2B, a genuinely good product is the biggest growth hack because customers talk and refer each other.
principles.quote: in the B2B space like having a good product is like the biggest growth hack, right?

principles.text: Founder personal brand and content can be the main acquisition channel; Oliver is hiring a full-time shadow writer to scale it.
principles.quote: I am my marketing. Like, dude, it's me like talking about it and tweeting it and talking about my journey and talking about case studies and success stories

principles.text: Build a business that grows on word of mouth instead of one that needs constant ad spend to buy revenue.
principles.quote: a business that can survive off of like word of mouth and grow off of word of mouth is a way more value business than like one where you need to like dump a dollar in to get like a $120 out

principles.text: High retainers make clients hypersensitive to results; a performance-based downsell converted far better and cut resentment.
principles.quote: when you charge people a lot of money like they're very sensitive to you like are you getting results you're not getting results

principles.text: Pure pay-per-result with zero upfront cost attracts tire kickers; adding a small monitoring fee filters for committed customers.
principles.quote: If you're willing to pay something then you'll be willing to take stuff down and got rid of the time wasters

principles.text: Zoom out on setbacks; short-term swings feel catastrophic but the long-run trend is what matters, so keep marching forward.
principles.quote: when you fixate on like a particular hour or moment or day sometimes it feels like it's like the end of the world.
